   About Ping Identity:   
 At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.  
 Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.  
 While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture.  We champion every identity.  One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.  
 We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.     Position Summary  
 We are seeking a Enterprise Account Executive to join Ping’s sales organization. The Enterprise Account Executive is responsible for driving new business while expanding the right existing relationships, helping customers solve complex identity challenges tied to security, digital experience, compliance, and operational efficiency. This role works across technical and executive buying groups and partners closely with cross-functional teams to turn identity priorities into measurable business outcomes. This draft follows Ping’s internal job description guide and reflects internal role signals showing a strategic team structure, strong new-logo expectations, and solution positioning across workforce, customer, and embedded identity use cases. 
  You Will  
 
 Own a strategic portfolio of enterprise accounts and build account plans that create, advance, and close high-value opportunities across enterprise, commercial, and technology organizations. 
 Generate pipeline through targeted prospecting, account prioritization, executive outreach, partner collaboration, and disciplined territory planning, with a strong emphasis on landing new logos. 
 Lead complex enterprise sales cycles from discovery through close, aligning Ping’s solutions to customer priorities around risk reduction, cost reduction, and improved digital experiences. 
 Position Ping’s identity platform across workforce, customer, and embedded use cases, including opportunities where technology companies integrate identity into their own products and experiences. 
 Build trusted relationships with security, IT, digital, product, operations, and executive stakeholders to shape buying consensus and move opportunities forward. 
 Partner closely with Sales Engineering, leadership, customer-success teams, and channel partners to develop account strategy, validate solution fit, and deliver a strong customer experience. 
 Maintain accurate pipeline, forecast, and account hygiene while operating with strong inspection, prioritization, and execution discipline. 
 Represent Ping with credibility in the market by connecting industry challenges to clear business value and differentiated identity outcomes. 
 
  You Have  
 
 4+ years of successful enterprise software, SaaS, cybersecurity, or identity sales experience, with a track record of exceeding quota in complex sales environments. 
 Experience selling into enterprise accounts, including commercial enterprises, technology companies, or adjacent regulated industries. 
 A demonstrated ability to generate pipeline and win net-new business through strategic prospecting and account planning. 
 Success navigating complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles that involve technical buyers, business leaders, and executive sponsors. 
 Strong business acumen and the ability to translate technical capabilities into value tied to revenue, efficiency, risk reduction, or customer experience. 
 Excellent communication, discovery, negotiation, and forecasting skills. 
 A disciplined, self-directed working style with strong prioritization and follow-through. 
 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. 
 
  Bonus Points If You Have  
 
 Experience selling identity, access management, CIAM, IGA, MFA, fraud, or verification solutions. 
 Familiarity with industry dynamics, including digital user or customer experiences, regulatory considerations, and security requirements. 
 Experience with platform, embedded, OEM, or ISV sales motions. 
 Experience working with strategic partners, GSIs, or channel ecosystems in enterprise accounts. 
 Knowledge of modern identity trends such as passwordless authentication, decentralized identity, or behavioral and risk-based security models.

  Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply.  Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications.   About Tailscale   
 Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.     About the Role   
 If you're passionate about solving complex technical problems and helping build trust between customers and engineering, this is the role for you. We're seeking a motivated Customer Reliability Engineer to join our team. You'll take ownership of our most complex, ambiguous customer escalations, solving issues where the root cause is not always obvious. You will work these issues to resolution or alternatively a fully-documented handoff that engineering can act on without delay. 
 As a Customer Reliability Engineer, you'll partner closely with the Customer Success Team, Support Team, and Product/Engineering to close the gap between "customer has described a problem" and "engineering has what it needs to fix it." This role reports directly to the Customer Reliability Engineer Team Lead. 
   Key Responsibilities   
 
 Own high-severity, post-sales technical escalations from intake through resolution or engineering handoff. This includes deep-dive investigations and reproduction of difficult-to-isolate bugs. 
 Get on calls with customers, pull logs, and communicate with the customer about leading theories. 
 Build engineering handoff packages that require minimal follow-up questions: reproducible case, log evidence (timestamps, node IDs), version matrix, impact scope, what's already been ruled out, and a proposed engineering team to own the fix. 
 File and track issues for confirmed bugs, keeping the ticket/issue link intact so engineering retains full customer context. 
 Monitor for patterns across escalations to catch recurring or systemic issues early; translate what you learn into product improvements, tooling, and runbooks that raise the technical bar for the whole Support org. 
 Partner with Support, CSE, and Product/Eng, while staying within this team's scope. 
 
   What We Are Looking For   
 
 4+ years in a technical support or escalation role at a SaaS or infrastructure company, with demonstrated ownership of escalated/enterprise-tier accounts. 
 A genuine problem-solver who gets energy from untangling hard, ambiguous technical issues 
 Comfortable owning a live, high-stakes customer call: staying calm, building trust, and communicating clearly with a frustrated or technical customer under pressure. 
 Hands-on networking experience in production or homelab environments: TCP/IP, routing, DNS, firewalls, NAT, VPNs, load balancers. 
 Deep familiarity with overlay networking concepts — WireGuard, UDP hole punching, STUN — and comparable VPN/networking products. 
 Code-level debugging capability: can read Go source, reason about goroutines/locks/channels, read pprof CPU/heap profiles, and understand network interface semantics. 
 Comfortable with infrastructure concepts: cloud IaaS, CI/CD pipelines, containerized applications, and Kubernetes debugging. 
 Strong systems administration skills as well as troubleshooting across Linux, macOS, and Windows. 
 Track record of independently building reproducible test cases and clear, evidence-backed bug reports engineering can act on directly.

jobs.title: Grafana Labs: Engineering Manager - Grafana Infrastructure (Remote, UK)
jobs.description:
Headquarters:  United Kingdom (Remote)
 

  Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at   grafana.com   and follow us on   LinkedIn   and   X  . 
 We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. 
 You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.   
 
  This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK, Spain or Ireland.  
 
 The Opportunity 
 About our platform 
 Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely. 
 The Foundations department owns the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP): the Kubernetes clusters, cloud service provider resources (CSP), hardware, identity, delivery, and observability systems that Grafana Labs's application engineers use to build, deploy, and run their workloads. 
 About the Infrastructure group 
 We're hiring an engineering manager for the Foundations Infrastructure group, which owns the cloud infrastructure Grafana Cloud runs on. The group provisions and operates Kubernetes clusters and CSP resources across GCP, AWS, and Azure; enforces identity, access, and security controls across those environments; and runs the observability and cost-visibility systems that keep the infrastructure measurable and accountable. 
 You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group. 
 We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. When a change is well communicated and understood, teams welcome it, and it lands as an improvement that makes the right way the easy way. You'll lead a squad that makes that happen. 
 How we work 
 Foundations is a global team that works asynchronously. The people who own a component or problem make the decisions about it, once stakeholders have had a chance to weigh in. Application teams build and run their own services; we give them a self-service platform to do it on. 
 Every engineer is on-call for the components their squad provides. We plan on-call, tactical work, and time off into every quarter, so roadmap work is roughly half of an engineer's time rather than all of it. 
 What You'll Be Doing 
 
 Hire, manage, and develop a squad of platform engineers, with regular feedback and career conversations that support each person's growth. 
 Own your squad's roadmap and quarterly objectives: help decide what the squad works on, what it defers, and why, across a broad remit where demand always exceeds capacity. 
 Take platform changes from design to fleet-wide adoption: staged rollouts, migration paths, and clear communication, so changes land well for the teams who depend on them. 
 Partner with the other Infrastructure squads on work that spans them, and with the teams across Foundations and the rest of Engineering whose work depends on yours. 
 Help shape how the group works as a whole, including planning, on-call, and the ownership model between squads. 
 Own the squad's intake. Requests, reviews, and support from application teams arrive continuously; keep them triaged and visible so that planned work still moves. 
 Keep on-call healthy: ensure a sustainable load and support incident response. 
 Work across team boundaries, contributing beyond your squad's scope where Foundations needs it.

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

Co-create the future with us  as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025.   An overview of this role  
 As a Candidate Experience Specialist, you'll shape how candidates experience GitLab from first touch through offer and handoff to our People Operations team. You'll be a key partner to Recruiters, hiring managers, and recruiting leadership, helping them execute hiring plans, coordinate interviews, and maintain accurate, transparent processes in our applicant tracking system and GitLab repositories. You'll act as a brand ambassador who embodies our values in every interaction, ensuring candidates receive timely, thoughtful communication and a consistent, high quality experience across a high volume of roles. You’ll focus on building strong relationships with hiring teams, improving and standardizing coordination workflows, and supporting GitLab's goal of hiring a qualified, diverse, and motivated team in our all-remote, global environment. 
  What You’ll Do    
 
 Collaborate with Recruiters, hiring teams, and Recruiting leadership to understand and execute the hiring plan for each job requisition. 
 Coordinate with Recruiters to maintain accurate, up-to-date hiring process information in the applicant tracking system and GitLab repositories.

We are looking for a Senior Manager, Pricing to define and lead Tines’ monetisation, pricing and broader commercial strategy. This role will research how customers perceive and realise value, identify the commercial models that best support our enterprise strategy, and translate that work into clear choices about how we package, price and sell our platform.

You will partner with Deal Desk, Product Marketing, Product, Finance, RevOps and Enablement to put decisions into practice, and build a small team of up to two people as the capability grows. 
  What You Will Be Doing  
 
 Define Tines’ monetisation, pricing and commercial strategy, connecting company and product strategy to clear choices about target customers, value metrics, packaging, price architecture and commercial models.

 Turn research and analysis into evidence-based recommendations for the Pricing Steering Committee. Make the strategic choices, economics, customer implications, risks and trade-offs clear, secure approval and maintain a record of decisions. 
 Own the pricing and commercial strategy roadmap and backlog. Establish a clear intake and prioritisation process, balancing foundational strategy, new monetisation opportunities, product launches and immediate deal needs.

 Measure the impact of monetisation, pricing and commercial decisions through indicators such as win rate, realised price, discounting, sales-cycle friction, package mix, adoption, expansion and renewal outcomes; use the learning to refine the strategy and roadmap. 
 Build the pricing and commercial strategy function over time, including hiring and developing up to two team members, defining ways of working and creating a trusted internal centre of expertise. 
 
  What You Bring With You  
 
 Deep commercial strategy experience in B2B SaaS, with a track record of researching markets and customer value, identifying monetisation opportunities and turning customer, market and financial evidence into clear strategic recommendations. 
 Experience creating or materially shaping commercial models, monetisation approaches, packaging or pricing strategy for a complex, sales-led business. Direct pricing specialism is useful, but not required. 
 Strong deal judgement. You can work with Sales and Deal Desk on strategic enterprise opportunities, understand the commercial trade-offs and balance the needs of an individual deal with the company’s broader strategy.

   Mission   Own and scale GNO's Meta ads from $50K+/month to $150K+/month, generating qualified calls that show up and close, within target cost per booked call and cost per acquisition. 
   About  GNO Partners    GNO helps Amazon brands scale and grow profits. Our founders built and exited two 7-figure Amazon brands. Since then, we've worked with 1,300+ brands, with 500+ active clients doing over $1B in combined sales, all run on a proprietary system we've built over 9 years. Meta is one of our main growth channels and we're ready to put real budget behind it.

You've personally run the accounts, made the calls and owned the numbers yourself, not "led a team that did it." You've built and scaled application (Direct App) and VSL call funnels for agencies, coaches or B2B service businesses. You'll own strategy and execution and work directly with the founders. 
 The major focus of this role is the ads themselves: ad strategy, ideation, copywriting, and creative. You'll come up with the angles, write the hooks and scripts, and drive what gets produced and tested. Media buying is a core part of the job too, but winning creative is what will move the numbers here. 
 Today we mainly run a Direct App funnel: ad → application → booked call. 
  Compensation  
 
 Base: $120K-$150K (negotiable, based on experience) 
 Commissions: $100K-$130K, tied to performance 
 OTE: $250K+ (uncapped) 
 Fully remote 
 
   What success looks like (first 3-6 months)   
 
 Hit the weekly qualified call targets agreed with the founders without tanking lead quality or show rate. 
 A steady pipeline of new ad concepts every week, built on angles, hooks and iterations of winners. 
 Scale spend from $50K+ toward $150K+/month while staying at CPBC & CAC KPI. 
 Tracking you trust: Pixel + CAPI + CRM, with 90%+ of booked calls tied back to the ad. 
 A structured testing engine with multiple meaningful tests per week across hooks, creatives, audiences and offers. 
 
  Responsibilities  
 
 Own ad strategy and creative: come up with angles, write ad copy, hooks and video scripts, brief production, and turn winners into new iterations. 
 Plan, build and manage Meta campaigns for: 
   Application and book-a-call funnels   
 Set up and maintain tracking (Pixel, CAPI, custom conversions, UTMs, offline events), and fix issues fast. 
 Own weekly reporting: KPIs, insights and a clear action plan. 
 Analyze the full funnel (impression → click → opt-in → booked → show → close) and fix what's broken, beyond "change targeting." 
 Work with the founders, creative and sales on new angles, offers and creatives. 
 Document structures, naming conventions and SOPs. 
 
  Requirements  
 
 3+ years running Meta ads for agencies, coaches or B2B service businesses. 
 Strong direct-response copywriting and creative strategy, with a portfolio of ads you wrote or ideated that scaled. 
 Personally managed $100K+/month on Meta for 12+ consecutive months. 
 Hands-on with call, application, or VSL funnels. 
 You think in pipeline metrics (show rate, close rate, CAC), not front-end CPL. 
 Solid tech: Events Manager, CAPI, custom conversions, UTMs, GA4/attribution (Hyros or similar is a plus), CRM (Pipedrive). 
 Excellent written English and clear, structured thinking.

Elkötelezettek vagyunk egy befogadó munkahelyi környezet kialakítása mellett, ahol mindenki, függetlenül származásától, nemi identitásától, szexuális irányultságától, életkorától, akadályoztatottságától, vallásától vagy hátterétől, kibontakozhat és a legjobbat hozhatja ki magából. Ha a jelentkezési folyamat bármely szakaszában szükséged lenne bármilyen jellegű támogatásra vagy segítségre, kérjük, hogy jelezd felénk. Elkötelezettek vagyunk amellett, hogy a jelentkezési folyamat mindenki számára elérhető legyen.  Originally posted on  Himalayas

jobs.title: AI Evaluator -  Flexible Hours
jobs.description:
Innodata  (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.   Scope of the Role:   At  Innodata , we’re partnering with the world’s leading technology companies to build the future of generative AI and large language models (LLMs). We’re on the lookout for smart, savvy, and curious Generative AI Specialist to join our global contributor community as part of our Subject Matter Expert (SME) on Demand program.  This is not a traditional full-time role. It’s a part-time, remote, flexible, project-specific opportunity designed for those who want to make a real impact—on their schedule. Whether you're a writer, linguist, educator, researcher, or just deeply passionate about language and logic, this role lets you contribute to cutting-edge AI development while maintaining control over your time.   You’ll be helping LLMs learn the intricacies of language and reasoning—not just how to write, but how to think. If you’ve ever dreamed of shaping the intelligence behind tomorrow’s technology, this is your chance.   This is more than just a gig—it’s a rare chance to help shape the future of AI from anywhere in the world, on your own terms.   What You’ll Own:  
 Rating/assessing the performance of AI models or algorithms based on their output or behavior through a set of evaluative questions.   
 Labeling elements of a piece of content rather than the content as a whole.   
 Assigning predefined categories or labels to items.   
 Evaluating the perceived quality and/or appropriateness of content   
 Generating labels to advance understanding of a concept, trend etc.   
 Creation of additional training data for machine learning models by applying transformations to the original data, such as modifying images (rotation, flipping, cropping), generating new text (paraphrasing, summarization), or altering audio/video signals (speed modification, pitch shifting) to reduce overfitting and increase dataset diversity.   
 Reviewing data and identifying whether or not a product feature works as intended based on the project's guidelines.   
 Labeling model outputs to identify if a piece of content is or isn't something. Examples: identify clickbait; identifying gaming videos; identifying branded content.  
 Ordering or ranking items based on a set of preferences or criteria.   
 Creating prompts or questions that will be used to generate responses from a language model or other AI system.   
 Projects that evaluate the relevance of content based on a relevancy scale (1-3, 1-5, etc.).   
 Generating responses to prompts or questions using a language model or other AI system.   
 Rewriting existing text while preserving the original meaning, often to improve clarity or style and adherence to guidelines.   
 Producing concise summaries of longer pieces of text or data.   
 Converting spoken language or audio content into written text.   
 Converting text or spoken language from one language to another.   
 Gathering and compiling various forms of data to be used for training, evaluating, or fine-tuning the AI models. This may include text, images, videos, audio files, or other types of digital content. 
  You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:  
 A Bachelor’s degree or higher in a  humanities specialization  is required. Advanced degrees are strongly preferred (Master’s or PhD) 
 Professional or Expert level proficiency (C1/C2) in English  
   The expected hourly salary range for this position is $15 p/hour, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.   
  Please be aware of recruitment scams involving individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent employers.  Innodata  will never ask for payment, banking details, or sensitive personal information during the application process. To learn more on how to recognize job scams, please visit the Federal Trade Commission’s guide at   
  If you believe you’ve been targeted by a recruitment scam, please report it to  Innodata  at    and consider reporting it to the FTC at   .

jobs.title: Registered Dietician - Part Time, Remote
jobs.description:
About  Clarity Pediatrics 
   Clarity Pediatrics  is reimagining pediatric chronic care, starting with ADHD. After successfully launching our virtual clinic for ADHD and anxiety, we are expanding our pediatric care platform to address other common chronic conditions and are focused right now on Obesity and Overweight management. Our clinical model is tech-enabled, backed by the best science, and designed to deliver exceptional health outcomes that transform a child's trajectory.  Our co-founders and leadership team have deep commitment to clinical excellence and domain expertise in healthcare. Our CEO, Christina LaMontagne, has led two startups and earned her MBA at Harvard Business School. Our Chief Medical Officer,Alesandro Larrazabal, MD, trained at UCSF and Stanford. Until recently, he was a Medical Director building specialty care services at Kaiser Permanente. Earlier, he worked at IDEO.  We're backed by top VCs who have supported category-defining health-tech companies like One Medical, Hims, Spring Health, Cityblock, Honor, and Tia.   The Role   For a lot of families, food is where the hardest moments of the day happen. ADHD medications can blunt appetite, picky eating can turn dinner into a standoff, and weight conversations can leave kids feeling judged. As our Registered Dietitian, you'll help families turn those moments into progress, with care that is practical, evidence-based, and free of stigma.  You'll join a true multidisciplinary team. Our physicians, nurse practitioners, and behavioral health clinicians treat together, so your nutrition plan isn't a referral that disappears into a chart. It's part of one coordinated plan for the whole child.  This is also a chance to build. You'll help design the evidence-based programming and protocols behind our nutrition care, from 1:1 visits to virtual group programs for kids and caregivers. If you've ever wanted to design the program instead of just running it, this is that role, on a part-time schedule you set.   What You'll Do    Care for kids and families (Practice Devotion to our Families)   
  Conduct 1:1 virtual nutrition visits for children and caregivers as part of our integrated care model.  
  Lead engaging virtual group sessions that give kids and caregivers practical tools they can use at the next meal.  
  Meet families where they are, with culturally responsive, non-stigmatizing language and plans that fit real budgets, schedules, and food traditions.  
   Deliver safe, high-quality care (Patient Safety Always Comes First)   
  Assess growth, intake, and medication effects such as appetite suppression, and flag concerns to the care team quickly.  
  Monitor progress, adjust recommendations, and document every interaction accurately and on time.  
  Work as one team (Earn Trust From Everyone)  
  Partner closely with our physicians, nurse practitioners, and behavioral health clinicians on shared, whole-child care plans.  
  Be a trusted voice for families and colleagues: clear, warm, and consistent.  
  Build what's next (Observe, Improve and Innovate)  
  Help design evidence-based nutrition programming and group curricula, drawing on pediatric nutrition research, family-based behavioral treatment, and motivational interviewing.  
  Share what you learn from families so we can keep improving the model, and help us measure what's working.  
   Who You Are (Play to Win)   
   A credentialed RD.  You hold an active RD or RDN credential through the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR).  
   Experienced with kids and families.  You have 3+ years of clinical or community nutrition experience, ideally in pediatric or family-focused settings.  
   Skilled in weight and metabolic health.  You've supported patients with obesity, overweight, or metabolic conditions, and you know how to talk about weight in ways that build trust instead of shame.  
   A confident group facilitator.  You can keep a virtual room of kids or caregivers engaged, and you enjoy it.  
   Comfortable with virtual care.  You use EMRs and telehealth platforms with ease and document efficiently.  
   Culturally responsive.  You've worked with families from diverse backgrounds and tailor your recommendations to their culture, resources, and goals.  
   A builder at heart.  You're energized by a fast-growing startup and happy to iterate on new care models.  
   Ready to serve our Medicaid families.  You're enrolled in California or Texas Medicaid, or willing to enroll.  
  Bonus points  
  State dietitian licensure, or openness to obtaining licenses with support from  Clarity Pediatrics  Medical Group.  
  Spanish fluency.  
   Compensation, Schedule and Benefits   The pay range for this role is 40–50 per hour, depending on experience. You're paid for all time worked, including visits, group sessions, prep, and documentation.  This is a part-time, hourly W-2 role, fully remote. You choose your hours within our operating window of Monday through Friday, 2pm–8pm PT. This role

 In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. In the bath that evening, he thought of a chocolate bar dispenser and swapped the chocolate for cash. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem. 
 Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. People do not read documentation, forgive a confusing screen, or care how the ledger works. They want one place that makes sense of everything — spending, saving, planning, investing — and that anticipates rather than reports: where they stand, what deserves attention, what to do next. Mercury is building personal banking* to that standard. 
 Personal Banking is how Mercury earns a place in someone's financial life. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving growth and engagement, and owning business performance. 
  *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

 Build a personal banking experience so good that people tell their friends and colleagues about it 
 Own the metrics, product strategy and the propositions we take to our customers, covering personal money management, banking, savings, investments, money movement, and in the future, lending

 Drive the use of AI in products where it makes the experience meaningfully better

 Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound,  including how personal banking connects to the businesses Mercury already serves

 A consumer product leader with taste: you have built products millions of people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work

 In 1851, a New York bookkeeper named George D. Lyman's fix: send everything through one central office and settle the net. On October 11, 1853, in the basement of 14 Wall Street, 52 banks cleared $22.6 million in a single sitting. Money between banks had stopped being an event and became seamless infrastructure.
